headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: a month-long slide has pushed Bitcoin under its 200-week line

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Hold the planned budget level. The long-run uptrend still counts, but Bitcoin is down about 13% in a week, about 10% under its 200-day average and now under its 200-week average, and a Rally watch drop window has been open since 13 November. Lead with trust and education, keep a reserve rather than raising spend, and only speed up after a close back above $72,928 (the 200-day average). This is a budget posture for planning, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($65,376) is about 10% under its 200-day average and 4% under the 200-week.
Up about 1% over 90 days, but down about 20% over the last 30.
The 200-day average ($72,928) is still rising, about 5% over 90 days.
Fear & Greed at 10 (extreme fear); 25 days under the 50-day average ($79,779).
watch: Bitcoin has dropped about 4% under its 200-week average ($68,100), the floor that held through recent weeks, and listed miner MARA says it will keep selling. A close back above $68,100 would steady the week, while a close below $64,150 (the 30-day low) would turn it clearly down.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run picture still leans up, but the last few weeks have turned clearly weak and Bitcoin has slipped under its last big floor. Short term, the mood is in deep fear: at about $65,376 Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 25 days, sits about 18% below it and about 22% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 10. An analyst quoted by PANews links the overnight drop to about $62,000 to a burst of concentrated selling in thin weekend trading, and Kava's security incident adds another safety worry. A normal week swings about $3,988, so a close above $68,100 (the 200-week average) would steady things, a close below $64,150 (the 30-day low) would turn the week clearly down, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messaging fits far better than promotion this week.

The next month is mixed and now leans slightly down, which is why the headline reads NEUTRAL even though the long-term trend is still up. The 90-day numbers still show price about 1% higher with most of those days above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 20%; news is pulling this a little lower too, as PANews reports miner MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin in six weeks and plans to sell more. Price is far under its 50-day average, so it must win back $79,779 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes for after it.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only just: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), while price is about 10% under it and about 48% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,928 (the 200-day average) again; $68,100 (the 200-week average) is the floor that just gave way, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A run of closes below the 200-week average would weaken this picture clearly and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.why: Bitcoin fell to about $62,000 overnight before bouncing, and an analyst quoted by PANews puts it down to concentrated selling in thin weekend trading rather than large holders leaving. BIT's analyst says the whole crypto market has lost about $800 billion of value since early October, and Glassnode reports stablecoin supply fell about $17 billion in a month, the most since 2022. Large coins fell together.
items.marketing_angle: A plain 'what happened this weekend' explainer fits better than any price-led campaign.

items.why: Several large holders are selling: miner MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin in six weeks, a B2C2-linked address has nearly emptied its LINK, and Solana treasury company Forward moved about $130 million of SOL to Coinbase Prime. On the other side, wallets linked to Erik Voorhees bought about $97 million of ETH in four days, and CryptoQuant says the largest wallets added about 47,000 BTC during the fall while mid-sized holders sold more.
items.marketing_angle: An education piece on why companies and funds sell or buy in a falling market is a timely topic.
